ScreenConnect: separate technician-client protection from compromise remediation

ConnectWise’s 11/12 18:45 UTC update identifies approximately 400 environments with RMM+ extensions for precautionary action, not confirmed compromises. Its current assessment finds no evidence of compromised ConnectWise infrastructure or a ScreenConnect vulnerability in initial access. Clients at 26.6.5 or later block the SCKit endpoint-to-technician spread technique, but do not remove existing compromises.

What to checkVerify the installed client on every technician workstation is 26.6.5 or later; keep the identified extensions disabled. Revoke web/IdP sessions from a trusted device and investigate with independent EDR or other out-of-band tooling. Preserve evidence, then clear queued commands/Toolbox items, unauthorized clients and persistence; validate before reconnecting.

ConnectWise Trust Center advisory

Rucio: SSH challenges accepted as authentication tokens enable administrator impersonation

SSH challenges are nonces for a later key exchange, but are stored alongside authentication tokens and not distinguished during validation. An unauthenticated caller can request a challenge for an arbitrary account and use it within its short lifetime to access APIs as that account, including an administrator. Exact affected and fixed branches are retained below.

What to checkUpdate rucio to a fixed release on its branch: 35.9.1 / 38.6.1 / 40.4.2 / 41.1.1 or later. Review API exposure, authentication and privileged operations. Keep nonces separate from authenticated credentials.

Active Storage: attachment alone can reach arbitrary file operations

Applications accepting untrusted uploads with mini_magick processing and a policy that permits the relevant ImageMagick coders may allow arbitrary file writes merely by attaching an image. Disk service additionally exposes files readable by the process. Preview generation and an explicit analyze call are not prerequisites.

What to checkUpdate activestorage to 8.0.5.2 / 8.1.4.1 and check mini_magick >= 5.1 and the effective policy. Check that overrides such as MiniMagick.cli_env do not bypass it. Rotate/revoke potentially exposed Disk service secret_key_base, master keys and external tokens; do not keep exposed secrets as fallbacks.

Aspire: an unauthenticated NotFound route is not fixed by a runtime update

The Aspire Dashboard NotFound route may allow unauthenticated telemetry deletion. Standalone browser-token deployments may also disclose the browser token; AppHost-hosted dashboards are affected too. Releases 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 are not fixed, and a .NET runtime/SDK update does not replace the Dashboard.

What to checkUpdate Dashboard to 13.6.5 or later. Replace container images and existing deployment manifests and redeploy. Check resolved Dashboard SDK packages, CLI bundles or custom paths selected by AppHost, then restart. A package-reference edit alone does not establish the running version.

Hono: mount and router path differences can bypass authentication middleware

Mount-prefix removal, re-normalization and RegExpRouter wildcard matching may reach inner handlers without the outer authentication middleware. Separate text/ping CSRF, multipart form validation and css-helper advisories retain their version details below.

What to checkUpdate hono to 4.13.16. Authenticate inside the mounted application; consider the documented TrieRouter workaround where needed. Regenerate PreparedRegExpRouter data and check custom patterns now rejected by the fixed router.

Hono Node adapter: proxy/application path disagreement and WebSocket DoS

A proxy may keep raw backslashes while the Node adapter normalizes them into separators, bypassing proxy path controls. This does not disable in-application authentication on the rewritten path. An ECONNRESET during asynchronous WebSocket upgrade is a separate process-crash issue.

What to checkCheck branch-specific @hono/node-server fixes: 1.19.18 / 2.1.6 for paths and 2.1.6 for the WebSocket issue. Verify proxy and application authentication. Updating core hono does not by itself update the adapter.

pgEdge RAG: ordinary concurrent queries can mix results across tenants

A shared BM25 index clears, populates and searches under separate locks, so ordinary concurrent unauthenticated queries can return another tenant’s documents. No injection or malformed input is needed. Separate advisories cover unbounded corpus reads and provider-key fragments in errors.

What to checkUpgrade the RAG Server product release to 2.0.0 or later. Go module first_patched_version values identify commits through pseudo-versions and differ from product releases. hybrid_enabled: false temporarily bypasses the shared index. The server’s own logs cannot retrospectively identify affected responses; rotate exposed provider credentials.

Pillow: pixel-count limits do not bound metadata processing

Overlapping TIFF/EXIF tag reads can make a small file consume excessive memory even with a tiny declared pixel count. A separate libtiff save issue lets metadata geometry disagree with the real image buffer, allowing memory reads/corruption and crashes.

What to checkUpdate Pillow to 13.0.0. Review TIFF saves, inherited exif/tiffinfo, Image.open and getexif paths, and bound worker memory/time. MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS alone does not prevent metadata-driven denial of service.

11/12 publication / date only; retrieval-time text · Publication/update confirmed

Air Terminal 6: OS command injection requires management login

JVN published this on 11/12. On v1.01.80 and earlier, a user able to log in to the web administration interface can execute commands as root. This is not an unauthenticated Internet-wide condition. The developer says fixed firmware has been deployed and disconnected devices update automatically on reconnection, so no user action is required.

What to checkCheck the official automatic-update conditions and device connectivity. Do not invent a fixed firmware number, which JVN does not list. Limit unnecessary management-interface access and shared credentials.

JVN coordinated disclosure

11/12 affected-scope revision / first published 11/09 · Publication/update confirmed

KUSANAGI: the 11/12 revision clarifies Nginx redirect scope

JVN published on 11/09 and revised affected scope on 11/12. CRLF handling in WordPress Nginx redirect rules can inject response headers when a crafted URL is visited. Affected: all KUSANAGI 7; all 8 Free/Business/Premium; 9 Security/Enterprise through 10.7.2-1 and Free/Business/Premium through 9.12.2-1. Apache httpd configurations are excluded.

What to checkCheck the edition and Nginx configuration, then apply the developer’s latest update or official workaround. Keep Apache exclusions explicit and do not infer a minimum fixed version absent from JVN.

JVN scope revision

11/12 JVN publication / notice of Apache 11/11 update · Publication/update confirmed

Apache HTTP Server: verify release 2.4.71 and deployed binaries

JVN’s 11/12 notice announces Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 for multiple issues in the 2.4 series. JVN delegates details to Apache advisories; this short notice alone does not establish every CVE prerequisite or exploitation status.

What to checkCheck official Apache advisories and distribution backports against enabled modules and running binaries. Distinguish an available update from the process running after restart.

Tailscale: minimum fixed version 1.104.4 for 4 official advisories

TS-2026-014–017 concern SSH Unix socket forwarding, SSH memory DoS, Serve Unix backends, and HTTP/2 capability confusion. The official bulletin specifies at least 1.104.4. A timing gap in changelog updates remains. Do not equate this with fixes for all 11 Tailworm items.

What to checkVerify 1.104.4 or later on production clients and check SSH/Serve usage conditions. To temporarily disable SSH forwarding, set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and restart the daemon. Do not include headscale or experimental connectors in the same fix scope.

Fireblocks mpc-lib: still no fix after assessment revision.

CERT VU701544 was revised on the 27th at 14:45 UTC. Descendant shares and chain codes may permit access to ancestor/root shares of the same MPC party, but this is not equivalent to obtaining a complete transfer key exceeding the threshold. Actual theft, amounts, and affected customer counts have not been disclosed.

What to checkTreat the fix as unavailable, protect chain codes as secrets, and investigate the entire hierarchy. Do not reuse Agent2.4.4 / SDK2.19.1 from the separate eMudhra incident as fixed versions for this vulnerability.

CVE-2026-41709 concerns actions left unlogged after administrator access, with a deadline of 11/11. Addition dates are not attack start dates; deadlines are requirements for US federal agencies.

What to checkCheck kernel and embedded-product updates, including the running version after restart. Use the ESX vendor response matrix and treat missing logs as an investigation limitation.

2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update · Publication or update confirmed

From PHP to the kernel and identity systems: observed artifacts and uncertainty

Dream’s report dated 10/26 describes artifacts of PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on 25 servers: 24 firewalls and an additional management server. It reports decrypted LDAP credentials and enumeration, but explicitly cannot determine whether password spraying, backdoor account creation or SAML key extraction succeeded. These are researcher observations without independent victim confirmation; direct evidence of AI code generation is also absent.

What to checkRestrict exposed management interfaces and update. Where compromise is suspected, investigate management servers, LDAP credentials, tunnels and identity logs. Do not infer undisclosed product names or affected versions.

Dream Research / CISA KEV

Struts REST: any-setter requires configuration as well as an update

In Struts 2 versions 7.2.1–7.3.0, @StrutsParameter restrictions do not cover REST @JsonAnySetter members. JVN advises updating to 7.4.0 or later and using struts.rest.anySetter.requireAnnotations=true with @StrutsParameter(allowDynamicKeys = true). Conditions include REST use and any-setter declarations; this does not establish compromise of all Struts applications.

What to checkCheck the update, configuration and annotations together. Work around the issue by avoiding any-setter or validating values in the application before storage.

Archive uploads are decompressed before namespace authorization and can consume server memory when reachable. Separately, callers knowing a run ID and suitable node information can retrieve logs with API-server permissions. External authentication and network controls affect reachability.

What to checkUpgrade the product to 2.18.0 and review readLog permissions in custom roles. The narrative identifies releases through 2.17.3; the API lists commit-based Go pseudo-versions, which are not product release numbers.

Issues include file creation or deletion by authenticated SQLite users, cookie-attribute injection through untrusted X-Forwarded-Prefix and XSS from hostile MySQL version strings. Observed CSRF tokens permit forgery, while version-cache poisoning causes persistent DoS. Code execution depends on additional conditions such as writing to a PHP-executable location.

What to checkUpgrade to 5.5.1 or later. Set trusted proxy prefixes and restrict database endpoints and PHP write permissions. Version 5.5.0 fixes the cache DoS alone; the other 6 require 5.5.1.

joserfc JWS and JWE resource guards are insufficient

Compact JWS copies segments before size checks, creating an additional input-sized allocation. General JSON JWE has no recipient-count bound and repeats RSA decryption per recipient; verify_all_recipients=False does not reduce that CPU work.

What to checkUpgrade to 1.7.6 or later to cover both issues and bound token sizes and recipient counts at application boundaries.

The publication window contains 92 npm malware advisories. This counts advisories, not machines or compromises. The table preserves package names and affected ranges from the original API; an unlisted first fix is not replaced with an assumed safe release.

What to checkCheck installation and execution history, lockfiles and distributed images. Isolate affected environments and revoke and reissue keys from a separate clean environment. Removal alone does not establish that persistence is gone; rebuild and investigate logs.

Arc: DuckDB aliases and tenant boundaries

The advisory reports cross-database reads by authenticated tokens through DuckDB I/O aliases within the shared storage root. Its prose describes an unresolved issue including 26.06.2, while the structured API names a fix-equivalent commit version; these claims conflict.

What to checkDo not infer resolution from the API fix field alone. Verify file access boundaries per database and restrict access to the shared root.

Affected configurations enable client uploads in @payloadcms/storage-vercel-blob and let authenticated users access the upload route. Configurations without client uploads are outside this path.

odf-kit: XSS through style attributes in converted documents

odtToHtml() and odsToHtml() interpolate unescaped style values. Inserting the output from a crafted document as HTML can execute script. Versions from 0.6.0 up to but excluding 0.14.2 are affected.

What to checkUpgrade to 0.14.2 or later and avoid directly displaying HTML from untrusted documents. Review previously converted output too.

GHSA-3cgg-c5pp-57h6

2026-11-03T20:29:16Z / GHSA publication / Prior context retained; narrative not rereviewed in this update · Publication/update confirmed

Stanza: nested pickle escapes weights_only checks

The lemmatizer in 1.14.0 performs unrestricted deserialization of compressed pickle inside a model. The advisory reports code execution as the loading user from an attacker-supplied lemma .pt. torch.load with weights_only=True does not inspect that inner pickle.

What to checkUpgrade to 1.15.0 and reject models of unknown origin. Investigate execution history and credential exposure in environments that already loaded them.

Elo: constructor access in JavaScript output

An attacker-controlled Elo string can reach host code execution when generated JavaScript is executed through unfiltered constructor access. This differs from the separate advisory about directly supplied AST objects.

What to checkUpgrade @enspirit/elo to 1.0.1. Do not execute code generated from untrusted input in a process with secrets or host privileges.

2026-11-03T17:51:30Z / GHSA publication / Prior context retained; narrative not rereviewed in this update · Publication/update confirmed

Elo: interpolation in generated Ruby

The Ruby backend does not sufficiently escape interpolation in emitted string literals and subtype-constraint labels. Running Ruby generated from crafted Elo can evaluate attacker-controlled expressions.

What to checkUpgrade @enspirit/elo to 1.0.1 and regenerate Ruby output. Safety of output from another backend does not establish safety of the Ruby output.

Elo: validation of programmatic AST input

Integrations that construct AST objects from JSON or plugins can pass unchecked fields into JavaScript, Ruby, Python or SQL output, enabling code injection. This input boundary differs from the normal string parser.

What to checkUpgrade @enspirit/elo to 1.0.1. Validate AST types and syntax and isolate generation and execution from untrusted ASTs.

  • @enspirit/elo (npm): affected <= 1.0.0 → fixed version 1.0.1

.NET Brotli: new indexing and existing remediation

This is a GHSA registration for the previously covered CVE-2026-111497. Exposure requires processing attacker-controlled Brotli data with decompression enabled; ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not enable this automatically by default. .NET Framework is unaffected.

What to checkApply the fixed version for each branch and package in the table, including 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14. Republish NativeAOT with the updated toolchain and verify distributed artifacts.

praktor: Telegram uploads cross workspace boundaries

In 0.9.0 and earlier, a Telegram document filename can write outside uploads within the persistent agent workspace. Overwritten instruction or configuration files can affect subsequent runs. This is not proof of arbitrary writes across the host.

What to checkUpgrade to 0.9.1 and restrict allowed Telegram user IDs. Review instructions, skills, hooks and upload history in existing volumes.

2026-11-03T17:24:27Z / GHSA publication / Prior context retained; narrative not rereviewed in this update · Publication/update confirmed

Keycloak: signature verification bypass in JWT Authorization Grant

An attacker with valid client credentials can exploit algorithm confusion in the JWT Authorization Grant flow to bypass signature verification and issue tokens for federated users linked to the affected Identity Provider. This does not establish an attack without credentials against every user.

What to checkUpgrade keycloak-services to 26.6.4. Review the affected flow, Identity Provider and client credentials and investigate unauthorized token issuance.

Metalama: code execution through same-user named pipes

Unrestricted deserialization over Visual Studio inter-process pipes can execute code. Writing requires code execution as the same Windows user already; this does not establish privilege escalation. The prose says no backports, while the API also lists 2025.1.18 and 2026.0.25 as fixes; the conflict is retained.

What to checkCheck Metalama 2026.1.19 and the maintained PostSharp extension 2026.1.5. Remove or migrate retired extensions and cross-check advisory and shipped releases for older branches.

Arc: logs route registered before authentication middleware

The advisory reports unauthenticated access to recent application logs because /api/v1/logs is registered before authentication middleware even with authentication enabled. Internal paths and database names may leak; retrieval of the bootstrap admin token was not confirmed.

What to checkPlace the logs route behind authentication and administrator authorization or block it if unused. Verify artifacts contain the fix commit in the table and review sensitive data in stored logs.

kaniko: Azure build tokens sent to lookalike registries

Untrusted Dockerfiles or build arguments can expose ARM access tokens when the build can obtain an Azure identity. Neither RUN nor push is required; using ACR is not a prerequisite. The fix is 1.25.20, but this repository publishes no binaries or images. The original acr-env module has no fixed release.

What to checkRebuild the executor, warmer and credential helper from 1.25.20 or later. Review Entra and Azure logs and identity permissions for suspect builds. Rotating credentials does not revoke issued tokens; investigate their remaining lifetime and any secrets the identity could read.

LXD: source authorization and DevLXD volume ownership

Cross-project instance and custom-volume copies check the destination without establishing permission to view the source. A separate DevLXD issue allows a guest with volume management enabled to read and write another guest’s volumes within the same project. These are different authorization boundaries.

What to checkReview copy permissions, source-project visibility and DevLXD volume-management settings. Restrict unnecessary guest permissions and investigate unexpected copies, device changes and secret access. Keep each advisory’s module boundary rather than reducing them to one release number.

In remote or auto VM cluster mode, the attacker must be able to create or modify a labelled Secret in a namespace readable by the proxy. The 11/6 KEV addition is CVE-2026-19868. A user with valid alternate-authentication credentials may bypass SAML controls and potentially SAML-enforced MFA. This is not a general credential-free MFA bypass. The retrieved official PSIRT page was only a JavaScript shell, so its body did not establish a minimum fixed version in this review.

What to checkCheck affected products, settings and fixes in the official SonicWall advisory and review alternate SSLVPN authentication and exposure. The KEV dueDate is 2026-11-20, not a legal deadline shared by every organization. Continue log review and credential assessment.

Keycloak: client-management roles reach JavaScript policies

Session state during client creation or import with authorization services enabled permits inline JavaScript policy upload restrictions to be bypassed. Authenticated delegated client-management privileges are required. Red Hat lists CVSS 9.1 and Important, marks packages Affected and supplies no fixed release. Its public_date is 2026-01-07, differing from this NVD registration date.

What to checkReview delegated manage-clients permissions, client imports and policy changes. Track product-specific Red Hat fixes without inventing a release. Default script restrictions alone do not establish protection against this path.

Fiber Admin: error-page configuration and a race condition

Before 4.0.1, an enabled custom database error page and a race with an administrator saving settings allow a request header to be written into a PHP file. Authentication is not required, but configuration and race prerequisites matter. WPScan lists 4.0.1 as fixed and 11/5 as initial publication.

What to checkUpdate to a release containing the 4.0.1 fix and inspect the custom database error-page setting and generated PHP files. Disabling a feature is distinct from completed patch deployment; correlate settings changes with access logs.

2026-11-08T02:13:00Z – 2026-11-08T15:53:00Z / NVD publication window / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · CNA record; preconditions require caution

OpenAM: notification WebSocket session-token exposure and SAML / self-registration authentication boundaries

In CVE-2026-123551 (from 14.0.0 before 16.1.4), an internal forward on legacy Liberty ID-FF endpoints reaches the notification WebSocket without authentication and exposes live iPlanetDirectoryPro tokens. In CVE-2026-123550 (before 16.1.4), ECP (PAOS) and HTTP-Artifact bindings accept unsigned assertions when WantAssertionsSigned is disabled. In CVE-2026-123549 (before 16.1.4), self-registration fails to enforce Valid Creation Attributes and permits joining administrative groups. The GitHub advisories were published on 10/22, distinct from this NVD registration date.

What to checkUpdate to 16.1.4 and inspect exposure of the notification WebSocket and Liberty ID-FF endpoints, SAML SP WantAssertionsSigned settings, and whether self-registration is enabled. Separate patch deployment from revoking and auditing existing sessions and unauthorized accounts.

2026-11-08T02:13:00Z – 2026-11-08T15:53:00Z / NVD publication window / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · CNA record; preconditions require caution

OpenEMR: 8.3.0 / 8.4.0 release-line fixes across SQL injection, file operations and OneTimeAuth

CVE-2026-124469 (Fee Sheet ORDER BY SQL injection) and CVE-2026-124450 (arbitrary file read/write via disposeDocument in the fax/sms module) affect versions before 8.3.0 and are fixed in 8.3.0. By contrast, CVE-2026-124445 (OneTimeAuth token replay and PIN brute force from 7.0.1 before 8.4.0) and CVE-2026-124467 (chained RCE via ESign router LFI and fax upload before 8.4.0) are fixed in 8.4.0. Updating only to 8.3.0 does not resolve the issues fixed in 8.4.0. Initial GitHub advisory publication occurred in months 8 and 9.

What to checkVerify a release at 8.4.0 or later and do not conflate 8.3.0 fixes with 8.4.0 fixes. Check whether the fax/sms and ESign modules are enabled, and investigate suspicious access to sqlconf.php, temporary upload paths and patient-portal token usage.

2026-11-08T02:13:00Z – 2026-11-08T15:53:00Z / NVD publication window / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · CNA record; preconditions require caution

Kyverno: cross-namespace boundary bypass via apiCall and variable generate targets

In CVE-2026-124440 (from 1.19.1 before 1.19.2), malformed percent-encoding bypasses the apiCall namespace clamp and allows calling cross-namespace or cluster-scoped APIs with the admission-controller ServiceAccount privileges. In CVE-2026-124441 (before 1.19.2), templating the generate rule's kind and namespace with variables skips authorization checks and allows creating resources in arbitrary namespaces via the background-controller. Both require permissions to create a Policy within a namespace.

What to checkUpdate to 1.19.2 and audit delegated namespaced Policy creation permissions, Policies using apiCall or variable generate rules, and creation history for unexpected MutatingWebhooks or RoleBindings.

Craft CMS: out-of-scope GraphQL reads and control-panel signing oracle

In CVE-2026-124427 (from 5.0.0 before 5.11.2), public GraphQL schemas or scoped tokens can traverse prev/next fields to read entries from out-of-scope sections. In CVE-2026-124430 (from 5.10.0 before 5.11.2), non-administrator control-panel users can obtain HMAC-signed Twig templates from app/render-elements and achieve code execution via the login redirect. Keep unauthenticated GraphQL prerequisites distinct from control-panel privilege prerequisites.

What to checkUpdate to 5.11.2. Review public GraphQL schema availability and token scopes, non-administrator control-panel permissions, and request logs for app/render-elements.

imgproxy: ICO loader integer overflow and staged fixes across 4.0.16 / 4.0.17

CVE-2026-123614 affects 4.0.0 before 4.0.16, where an ICO data_size integer overflow causes heap corruption and RCE, fixed in 4.0.16. Meanwhile, CVE-2026-123615 affects 3.3.0 before 4.0.17, where BMP header reconstruction on a small ICO data buffer causes out-of-bounds heap read/write, fixed in 4.0.17. Because CVE-2026-123615 remains present in 4.0.16, do not conflate affected and fixed releases.

What to checkUpdate to 4.0.17 or later. Do not treat 4.0.16 as a complete fix for both CVEs; inspect routes that accept external image URLs and check worker crash history.

Hickory DNS: DNSSEC validation bypass and unpatched legacy hickory-proto range

CVE-2026-123587 affects hickory-net from 0.26.0 before 0.26.2, permitting wraparound NSEC nonexistence forgery via comparison against an unvalidated SOA record. CVE-2026-123605 fails to verify that the RRSIG Signer's Name matches the target RRset's zone, permitting signatures from another zone's key; while hickory-net is fixed in 0.26.2, legacy hickory-proto 0.1 through 0.25.0-alpha.3 lists Patched versions as None (unprovided) in the GitHub advisory.

What to checkUpdate hickory-net to 0.26.2 or later. Note explicitly that legacy hickory-proto 0.1 through 0.25.0-alpha.3 has no in-series fixed release and requires migrating to hickory-net 0.26.2 or later; review dependency trees that rely on DNSSEC validation.

Initial IBM bulletin publication occurred on 10/29 and 10/27, distinct from this NVD registration date.

IBM Bob Shell and Langflow OSS: automatic MCP execution and local isolation bypass

IBM Bob Shell 1.0.4 through 2.0.1 (CVE-2026-9764) automatically executes workspace MCP server configurations without user consent when opening an untrusted repository, fixed in 2.0.2 via Workspace Folder Trust. The IBM bulletin explicitly states that opening only trusted repositories is partial (do not fully address). Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.12.2 (CVE-2026-97677) allows authenticated flow authors to bypass local file isolation and read/write configuration, secret and database files, fixed in 1.12.3.

What to checkUpdate IBM Bob Shell to 2.0.2 or later and Langflow OSS to 1.12.3 or later. Do not treat operational precautions as a complete fix; inspect MCP configurations in previously opened repositories and check Langflow data directories and secrets for exposure.

AI/MCP: loopback trust, shell exposure and workspace boundaries

GPUStack loopback auto-admin can be reached through a same-host reverse proxy or forged header; fixed in 2.2.0, with reported exploitation and a KEV addition. fast-agent-mcp through 0.7.20 exposes unauthenticated HTTP; --shell adds RCE, fixed in 0.7.21. The macOS Claude Code Edit race requires attacker code inside the sandbox; fixed in 2.1.251. These advisories have independent conditions. This publication window contains 13 advisories.

What to checkUpgrade GPUStack to 2.2.0 or later and audit API keys and worker secrets. Check MCP binding, authentication and shell capabilities, and use each package table for fixes. Agent/workspace findings alone do not establish a compromised host.

Kubernetes: shared cache, pipeline authorization and session ownership

Kubeflow Pipelines legacy V1/raw-Argo caching can disclose or substitute outputs across namespaces. Standard V2 caching is outside that advisory. Distinguish fixed release 2.18.0 from the Go pseudo-version table. Telepresence Traffic Manager authentication and tunnel session ownership are separate advisories. This publication window contains 8 advisories.

What to checkConfirm all old Kubeflow cache-server processes have exited and new replicas enforce isolation. Adding namespace to a key alone is insufficient. Review pipeline sharing, network reachability, Telepresence sessions and exposed secrets.
